skill.displayName: Frog Skin Moisture Assessment | 蛙类皮肤湿润度评估

llm.summary: The skill is a cloud-backed frog media analyzer, but it automatically handles identity, uploads media or URLs, queries cloud history, and persists service tokens without enough user control or disclosure.

dimensions.detail: The runtime reads workspace identity material from data/smyx-api-key.txt, creates or reuses a workspace data directory and SQLite database, sends identity fields to external lifeemergence endpoints, and uploads local files or forwards URLs for analysis.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains Python scripts, YAML config, and requirements files; I found no install hook, shell persistence setup, or destructive install behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions use default/automatic triggers for media analysis and history lookup and require cloud API use, which can send user-provided media or retrieve cloud report history with limited fresh confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common DAO stores user records plus token and open_token fields in a local SQLite database and silently reuses or provisions default identities, with no clear user-facing revocation or consent flow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The frog skin moisture analysis purpose is broadly coherent with cloud AI analysis, local file or URL input, video support, and historical report listing because SKILL.md discloses those capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this only if you are comfortable sending frog images/videos or URLs, internal identity values, and report-history requests to the configured lifeemergence.com services, and with the skill caching service tokens in the workspace data directory. Prefer non-sensitive media and confirm how cloud retention, account deletion, and token revocation are handled.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic getattr filters are real in the generic DAO, but I did not find evidence they are exposed directly to arbitrary user-controlled filter input in this skill path; this is a code-hardening issue rather than a core verdict driver.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill documentation discloses scripts, network APIs, file input, and cloud history, but there is no explicit permission boundary for network transfer, local identity reads, local token persistence, or output file writes.
[TP4] expected: The scanner's purpose mismatch is partly downgraded because SKILL.md explicitly lists image/video, local files, URLs, cloud history, and internal identity handling; the remaining concern is under-scoped privacy disclosure, not hidden unrelated functionality.
[SDI-1] expected: Video/URL handling and report-listing are documented in SKILL.md, but the bundled shared user-management and token persistence code is broader than the narrow frog-assessment task needs.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Identity resolution, reading data/smyx-api-key.txt, automatic phoneLogin/register calls, and local token storage are artifact-backed and materially under-disclosed for a media-analysis skill.
[SDI-4] expected: Generic video-analysis wording exists in the shared smyx_analysis module, but the top-level frog script and SKILL.md specialize the user-facing workflow to frog skin moisture assessment.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The default analysis trigger and automatic history-query trigger are real and may cause cloud analysis or report retrieval with weaker user scoping than a sensitive media/history workflow should have.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The skill reads local media into memory for upload or forwards remote URLs, and the shared utility silently attaches identity/auth headers and reads workspace identity state; these behaviors need clearer disclosure and consent.
[E1] unexpected: The outbound phoneLogin/register request sends openId, mobile, and source to an external health endpoint; authentication is coherent with the cloud service but the identity transfer is not clearly surfaced to users.
[P2] expected: The reported hidden character is a zero-width joiner inside an emoji sequence in SKILL.md, not an operative hidden instruction or prompt-injection payload.
[YR4] expected: I found no metadata-poisoning instruction beyond the ordinary YAML front matter and the emoji-related zero-width joiner; this finding is not a verdict driver.
